*   **Time Complexity**: Dominated by the tetrahedralization step ($O(N \log N)$ or similar depending on the algorithm) and the marching tetrahedra step ($O(T)$ where $T$ is the number of tetrahedra).
Rendering is $O(P)$ where $P$ is the number of pixels.
The method is iterative, so total time is proportional to the number of iterations.
*   **Memory Complexity**: $O(N + T + P)$.
Stores point positions, SDF, SH coefficients, tetrahedra, and rendered buffers.
*   **Measured Performance**: Not given in the sources.
Resampling allows dynamic adjustment of $N$ to balance detail and performance.
*   **Strengths**: Joint optimization of geometry and appearance; flexible topology updates; differentiable rendering allows gradient-based optimization from 2D cues.

*   **Limitations**: Computationally expensive due to repeated tetrahedralization and marching tetrahedra; sensitive to initialization and hyperparameters (e.g., `accumulation_delaunay`); requires multi-view inputs.
*   **When to use**: When reconstructing 3D meshes from multi-view images with implicit surface representations and differentiable rendering is desired.
*   **When not to use**: When real-time performance is critical or only single-view input is available.
The TetWeave Optimization Pipeline is part of the TetWeave framework, which uses tetrahedralization for implicit surface reconstruction.
The method leverages differentiable rendering to optimize a set of points and their associated scalar fields to match 2D image observations.
